notes.gdp: GDP is Eurostat's quarterly national accounts, seasonally and calendar adjusted. Figures before Lithuania joined the euro in 2015 are converted from litas at the fixed rate of 3.45280 litas per euro.
notes.inflation: Inflation is the EU's harmonised index (HICP), the measure the ECB targets; the State Data Agency also publishes a national CPI, which can differ by a few tenths. Lithuania joined the euro on 1 January 2015 and has had no policy rate of its own since: the rate shown is the European Central Bank's deposit facility rate, from that date. Before 2015 the litas ran on a currency board run by the Bank of Lithuania, tied to the US dollar until 2002 and to the euro after, which is not shown.
notes.labour: Unemployment is Eurostat's monthly, seasonally adjusted rate (ILO definition, ages 15 to 74). The Employment Service's registered unemployment rate, sometimes quoted in Lithuanian news, is a different measure. Employment and participation rates are Eurostat's seasonally adjusted Labour Force Survey figures for ages 15 to 64, from 2009.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Eurostat's monthly total with the rest of the world, in euros. Lithuania usually imports more goods than it exports.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are Eurostat's excessive deficit procedure figures for general government, calendar years, so the latest year is a year ahead of the IMF's.
notes.markets: The 10-year yield is Eurostat's monthly long-term interest rate for convergence purposes (the EU's benchmark Lithuanian government yield), which runs about a month behind. Lithuania's benchmark bond trades thinly, so the published rate often stays unchanged for months at a time. The exchange rates are the Federal Reserve's daily euro rates, shared with every euro area page.
